findings.title: An unanswered 'Korean school' answer is not limited by the answered education, so professional visas open for high-school readers
findings.repro: Page link #nationality=UZ&age=30&edu=1&experience=0&path=NONE (edu = high school, the optional 'Highest level completed in Korea' left blank, which is the form default). The built page and sim.options() both show E-7-1, E-7-2, E-7-3, E-3, D-10-1 and D-10-2 as OPEN at L1. Adding koreanEdu=0 blocks all six (reasons edu, experience, koreanEdu). Same cause: {edu:3} on NONE>E-7-1>F-2-7 leaves F-5-15 (needs {koreanEdu:5}, a Korean doctorate) open. The {koreanEdu:2} and {koreanEdu:4} alternatives return 'maybe' because checkFact's LEVELS branch only looks at facts.min when koreanEdu is undefined.
findings.expected: koreanEdu is the highest level completed in Korea (i18n vm_korean_edu), so it can never exceed edu. When edu is known (facts.known.edu, already raised by the path's gives) and is below the wanted koreanEdu, the check should return 'no'. A high-school reader with no experience should see E-7-1 and the other options above as blocked.
findings.fix: In checkFact, before `return facts.min[key] >= want ? 'yes' : 'maybe';`, add: `if (key === 'koreanEdu' && have === undefined && facts.known.edu !== undefined && facts.known.edu < want) return 'no';`

findings.title: The 'minors only' parent fact uses today's age, not the age at the step, so an adult on the path still matches family-of-F-5 visas
findings.repro: sim.options({nationality:'UZ', age:17, spouse:'none', parent:'f5', edu:1}, ['NONE','D-2-2'], 2): F-2-3 is open with tag {key:'matches'}, at age [19, 23]. With parent:'foreigner' instead, F-3 is open with 'matches'. Confirmed in the built page (#nationality=UZ&age=17&spouse=none&parent=f5&edu=1&path=NONE.D-2-2 shows 'F-2-3 ✓ Matches your details'). A reader aged 19 today on the same path gets both options BLOCKED (spouse, parent).
findings.expected: profileFacts drops the parent answer at 19 ('parents' status matters for minors only'). The time-along-path feature makes this reader at least 19 when they take the step, so F-2-3/F-3 (and F-2-71, F-2-81, F-2-13, F-2-T1) should no longer open through the parent alternative or be tagged as a match.
findings.fix: In factsAt, once `age` is computed, add `if (age[0] >= 19) known.parent = 'none';`. Apply the same age-at-step rule to the `own` facts used for 'matches' in assess, instead of `person.age` in profileFacts.

findings.title: STEM status (and rank) from the reader's current degree, or forced to false, blocks STEM options for degrees earned on the path
findings.repro: A 15-year-old who picks education 'below high school': readDetails (visamap.js:180) sets stem:false without asking. sim.options({nationality:'UZ', age:15, edu:0, koreanEdu:0, stem:false}, ['NONE','D-4-3','D-2-2','D-2-3'], 4) gives F-2-7S BLOCKED [stem] (shown as an education reason), although the path has just given a Korean master's (koreanEdu 4). The same reader with edu left blank gets F-2-7S open. An adult {edu:3, koreanEdu:0, stem:false} on NONE>D-2-3 also gets F-2-7S BLOCKED [stem] after a Korean master's.
findings.expected: Like rank, stem describes the reader's existing degree, and for edu < 1 it was never asked. Once the path gives a higher degree (D-2-x gives edu/koreanEdu), the field of that new degree is unknown, so F-2-7S (and D-2-5, D-10-3) should read 'maybe', not 'no'.
findings.fix: In visamap.js readDetails, use `details.stem = extras ? yes('stem') : undefined;` (as is already done for rank). In factsAt, when a visa's gives.edu raises edu above the reader's answer, delete known.stem and known.rank so they become unknown.

findings.title: Income 'not yet' ignores reductions and asset routes the map cannot decide
findings.repro: F-5-6: {nationality:'UZ', age:30, korean:true, edu:1, koreanEdu:0, income:20}, path NONE>F-4 gives income.result 'later' and tag '⏳ Income ₩52.4M+' (option marked NOT YET). With kiip:5 answered, the same reader gets result 'maybe' and no tag: at 70% the requirement is ₩36.7M and the own half (₩18.3M) is already met. F-5-14: {korean:true, income:10} on H-2>F-4 gives 'later' while the same line says 'May be lower: a listed technical or skills licence instead of income' (factor 0). F-5-16 / F-5-9 / F-5-15 with own income below the amount give 'later' (e.g. income 60 on NONE>E-7-1>F-2-7: '⏳ Income ₩104.8M+'), although the rule and its how text offer assets as an alternative ('Or household net assets of ₩707.2M or more instead').
findings.expected: The engine's own rule is that an unknown beats a sure 'not yet', and an unanswered fact never counts against the reader. When a 'maybe' reduction would make the reader's income enough, or the rule has an assets route the map never asks about, the result should be 'maybe', not 'later'.
findings.fix: Only return 'later' when no unknown can help. Compute the amount at the lowest factor among the 'maybe' cuts (respecting floor), apply the same own/half test to it, and only return 'later' if it still fails and `rule.assets` is not set; otherwise return 'maybe'.

findings.title: Requirement shown rounded down, so a reader at the displayed amount is told 'not yet'
findings.repro: #nationality=UZ&age=30&edu=3&income=52.4&path=NONE.E-7-1.F-2-7.F-5-10. The page states 'Income: ₩52.4M a year or more (1× GNI per person for 2025)' and the option is tagged '⏳ Income ₩52.4M+' (NOT YET), because rules.js:255 compares 52.4 >= 52.416. The same happens at 104.8 for 2× GNI (104.832), 157.2 for 3× GNI, 41.9 for 80% and 31.4 for 60%.
findings.expected: The amount shown as the threshold should never be lower than the real threshold, or a reader whose entered income equals the shown amount should not see 'not yet'.
findings.fix: Round requirement amounts up when formatting them, e.g. money(Math.ceil(amount * 10) / 10) for income requirements (the laterIncome tag and the incomeLine amounts), so 52.416 shows as ₩52.5M.

findings.title: Under the own-half rule the 'not yet' tag names the household total, not the missing own share
findings.repro: F-5-6 with {korean:true, edu:1, koreanEdu:0, kiip:0, income:20} on NONE>F-4: result is 'later' only because own 20 < 52.416/2, yet the tag reads '⏳ Income ₩52.4M+'. A reader with ₩20M own and ₩40M spouse income (household ₩60M) is told they need ₩52.4M, which their household already has. What they lack is ₩26.2M of their own.
findings.expected: When 'later' comes from the ownHalf rule, the tag should show the own-share amount (amount / 2), with wording that it is the reader's own income.
findings.fix: In incomeFor, return the amount that failed (e.g. `needOwn: halfRule ? amount / 2 : amount`). In assess, use it for the laterIncome tag, or use a distinct tag key for the own-half case.

findings.title: An unanswered 'Highest level completed in Korea' is no longer capped by the reader's education, so Korean-degree-only options show as open to readers with less education
findings.repro: In the form choose Uzbekistan, age 30, current visa E-7-1, Highest completed education = High school, and leave 'Highest level completed in Korea' on Not specified (the default). Same as opening /en/visa-map/#nationality=UZ&age=30&edu=1&path=E-7-1. Row 1 shows E-3 (Researcher, needs koreanEdu 4) and F-5-15 'Korean doctorate holder' (needs koreanEdu 5) as open options with no tag. With koreanEdu=0 the same page blocks both with 'Education doesn't match'. Before this change the page set koreanEdu = edu or 0 whenever edu was given, so these options were always closed. Across all visas a high-school reader now also sees F-2-7, F-2-7S and D-9-5 open. A related case: edu=3&koreanEdu=5 (the select accepts a Korean level above the overall one) gives F-5-15 and E-3 the tag '✓ Matches your details', while F-5-9 (foreign doctorate) is blocked.
findings.expected: A Korean level can never be higher than the highest education the reader gave. With edu=1 or edu=3, options that need koreanEdu 4 or 5 should be blocked ('Education doesn't match'), unless the path itself gives that degree (D-2-x gives). Leaving the select unset should only keep levels up to edu open.
findings.fix: In checkFact, before the LEVELS branch, add: `if (key === 'koreanEdu' && have === undefined && facts.known.edu !== undefined && facts.known.edu < want && !(facts.min.koreanEdu >= want)) return 'no';` (known.edu already includes what the path gives). In visamap.js readDetails (line 179), cap an answered value: `const k = level('koreanEdu'); details.koreanEdu = extras ? (k === undefined ? undefined : Math.min(k, details.edu)) : 0;`

findings.title: Branch memory brings back steps the reader cleared by reopening a visa
findings.repro: Open /en/visa-map/#nationality=UZ&age=24&edu=3&path=NONE.E-7-1.F-2-7.F-5-16, then click: row 1 D-10-1 (path NONE.D-10-1); row 1 E-7-1 (restored to NONE.E-7-1.F-2-7.F-5-16, correct); row 1 E-7-1 again to reopen (NONE.E-7-1); row 1 D-10-1 (NONE.D-10-1); row 1 E-7-1. The path comes back as NONE.E-7-1.F-2-7.F-5-16. When the reader last left E-7-1, nothing was chosen after it, because they had cleared F-2-7 > F-5-16 by reopening. The reopen-at-level-2 variant correctly brings back only NONE.E-7-1.F-2-7, so the two cases behave differently.
findings.expected: Picking E-7-1 again brings back what was chosen after it the last time it was left, which here is nothing: NONE.E-7-1 with the row after it open.
findings.fix: Store an empty tail too when a visa is replaced: `const key = path.slice(0, cut + 1).join('.'); if (path.length > cut + 1) tails.set(key, path.slice(cut + 1)); else if (!reopen) tails.delete(key);`

findings.title: Income box accepts amounts above its max (e.g. salary typed in won), and every income check then passes
findings.repro: In the form enter Uzbekistan, age 30, visa E-7-1, and 45000000 in 'Yearly income in Korea, ₩ million' (the salary in won). The browser marks the field invalid (validity.rangeOverflow, max=10000), but the form is novalidate and amount() only rejects negative numbers. The map draws with the profile line 'Income: ₩45,000,000M'. The F-2-T how text says 'Income: ₩104.8M a year or more … ✓ Your income is enough.' and all '⏳ Income …' tags disappear.
findings.expected: An amount outside the box's range is treated as unknown, as the comment above amount() says ('not a sensible amount is unknown'), or the form shows an error. It should not count as a ₩45 trillion income.
findings.fix: In amount(), also reject values above the input's max: `return Number.isFinite(value) && value >= 0 && value <= Number(f[name].max || Infinity) ? value : undefined;` (or use `f[name].validity.valid`).

findings.title: Desktop form: income hint pushes the Work experience select out of line with the income input
findings.repro: Open /en/visa-map/ (or /ru/) at 1280px wide and open 'Personalize your map'. In 'Work and investment', the income input sits at top=558 and the Work experience select at top=626, level with the income hint text instead of the income box. The row is .vm-row-inputs (align-items: end, blog.css:941) and only the new income field has a hint under its input, so bottom alignment lines the experience select up with the end of the hint.
findings.expected: The experience select and the income input line up, as the other .vm-row-inputs rows do (TOPIK/KIIP, nationality/age).
findings.fix: Give the income field its own row: move the income <div class="vm-field"> (lines 296-301) out into a separate <div class="vm-row"> after the experience/invest row. Alternatively, drop vm-row-inputs from the row at line 286.

findings.title: Uzbek page mixes decimal separators: generated amounts use '.', data texts use ','
findings.repro: Open /visa-map/#nationality=UZ&age=40&income=60&path=B-1.F-6-1 (Uzbek is the default language) in Chromium. The selected F-6-1 how text reads '…yillik daromadi ikki kishi uchun taxminan ₩25,2 mln…' (from data) and then 'Taklif qiluvchining daromadi: yiliga ₩25.2 mln…' (from money()). All generated amounts on the uz page use a dot ('₩104.8 mln', '0.7× GNI'). Chromium's Intl.NumberFormat('uz') formats 104.8 as '104.8', while ru and uz-Cyrl give '104,8' and the hand-written uz data uses commas.
findings.expected: One decimal separator on the Uzbek page, the comma used everywhere else in the uz texts: '₩25,2 mln', '₩104,8 mln', '0,7× GNI'.
findings.fix: Don't rely on the browser's 'uz' locale data. For example, format with a locale that gives a comma (`page.lang === 'uz' ? 'uz-Cyrl' : page.langTag`) in money() and in the incomeGni formatter at line 105, or take the decimal separator from an i18n string.

findings.title: README says the scenario tests cover path memory, but no test does
findings.repro: The README says '`scenarios.test.mjs` walks real paths (path memory, the F-2/F-5 income rules and their reductions)'. grep -n 'memory\|tails\|follow' tests/*.mjs finds nothing. The path-memory logic (tails/follow) lives only in assets/js/visamap.js, which no test imports. The defect in the branch-memory finding above passes the whole 50-test suite.
findings.expected: Either a test covers the switch-and-back / reopen behaviour, or the README stops claiming path memory is tested.
findings.fix: Remove 'path memory, ' from README.md line 37, or move the tails/follow logic into rules.js (or a small module) and add a scenario test for it.

findings.title: F-2-T: readers who meet only the degree or only the career criterion get the 3x (or 2x) amount and 'Your income is enough', but the rule needs 4x GNI
findings.repro: I opened the built page /en/visa-map/#nationality=UZ&age=35&edu=4&rank=3&experience=0&income=160&path=NONE.F-2-T (top-100 degree, no career). The F-2-T card's how text says '(4× GNI if you miss the degree or the career criterion)', then the computed line says 'Income: ₩157.2M a year or more (3× GNI per person for 2025). ✓ Your income is enough.' A career-only reader (edu=2&experience=8&income=160) gets the same ✓. As a change in Korea, path=E-1.F-2-T with edu=4&rank=3&experience=0&income=110 shows 'If you meet the Top-Tier criteria. Income: ₩104.8M a year or more (2× GNI per person for 2025). ✓ Your income is enough.' F-2-7.F-2-T behaves the same. In sim, rules.incomeFor returns amount 157.248 or 104.832 with result 'yes'. The needs union [{edu:4,rank:3},{experience:8},{edu:5,experience:5}] lets one-leg readers through, and incomeFor always applies {gni:3} (or the move's {gni:2}).
findings.expected: check_R1 #36 and check_R4b #24 (고시 2025-86 제4조) say an applicant missing the degree leg or the career leg needs at least 4× GNI (₩209,664,000). The 2× in-Korea route needs every criterion except income, so both degree and career. These readers need ₩209.7M. With ₩160M or ₩110M the page must not say their income is enough.
findings.fix: Give F-2-T's income a full-criteria condition and a 4x fallback. For example, set income: {gni: 3, full: [{edu: 4, rank: 3, experience: 8}, {edu: 5, rank: 3, experience: 5}], otherwise: 4}. In rules.incomeFor, use gni = rule.otherwise when checkNeeds(person, rule.full, facts).result === 'no'. Use the same full/otherwise on the {gni: 2} moves at lines 912, 984, 1140, 1347 and 1726. At minimum, suppress the ✓ for F-2-T when the full alternative is not met.

findings.title: E-7-S2 -> F-2-T note promises 2x GNI but the move has no income override, so the card shows 3x and marks it 'not yet' (E-7-S1 -> F-2-T has the same gap)
findings.repro: /en/visa-map/#nationality=UZ&age=30&edu=5&rank=3&experience=8&income=120&path=E-7-S2.F-2-T shows the F-2-T card as '[✓ Matches your details|⏳ Income ₩157.2M+] ... 1+ year in a high-tech field in Korea: an income of 2× GNI (instead of 3×) and a ministry recommendation are enough. Income: ₩157.2M a year or more (3× GNI per person for 2025).' The move added in this diff (E-7-S1 -> F-2-T, line 1284) also gets 3× and '⏳ Income ₩157.2M+' for a ₩120M earner. Its siblings E-1, E-3, E-7-1, E-7-T and F-2-7 -> F-2-T all carry income: {gni: 2}. ops.json e7-special#1 itself warns that without the override the card would show 3× next to a 2× note.
findings.expected: The in-Korea change from D-7..E-7 after 1+ year in a high-tech field asks 2× GNI (₩104,832,000); see R1 #36, R4b #24 and check_R4b #9. With ₩120M the reader meets the bar: the card should say ₩104.8M with no ⏳.
findings.fix: Add `income: {gni: 2}` under `- to: F-2-T` in E-7-S2.next (line 1316) and in E-7-S1.next (line 1284).

findings.title: F-2-3: a minor child of an F-5 holder is shown the sponsor's 1x GNI income test, which applies only to spouse invitations
findings.repro: /en/visa-map/#nationality=UZ&age=15&parent=f5&path=F-1.F-2-3 shows the F-2-3 card as '...no income test for a minor child. Your sponsor's income: ₩52.4M a year or more (1× GNI per person for 2025). May be lower: a household of 3 people or fewer: 70%.' path=NONE.F-2-3 shows the move note at line 2193, 'Spouse or minor child of an F-5 holder, whose household earns at least 1× GNI (70% for up to 3 people). A minor child applies with a visa confirmation (CCVI)...', and the same ₩52.4M line. The same happens in ru, for example 'Доход приглашающего: от ₩52,4 млн'. In sim, incomeFor gives base 52.416, whose 'sponsor', for age 10 with parent f5.
findings.expected: R4b #32 (confirmed), R5 #11 and check_R1 #38 agree: notice 2015-2 covers marriage-cohabitation (spouse) invitations only, and the minor-child change list has no income document. The card should say there is no income test for the child.
findings.fix: Add an incomeCuts entry such as `minorChild: {factor: 0, when: [{parent: f5}], text: {en: 'no income test for a minor child', ...}}` and list it in F-2-3's `cuts`. Rewrite the NONE -> F-2-3 note (line 2193) to say: 'To invite a spouse, the F-5 holder's household needs 1× GNI (70% for up to 3 people); no income test for a minor child.'

findings.title: The income 'not yet' verdict ignores reductions the engine itself lists as possible, so blank answers make the result worse
findings.repro: A reader with Korean roots on F-4, age 45, income ₩30M, goes to F-5-14 (/en/visa-map/#nationality=UZ&age=45&korean=yes&income=30&path=F-4.F-5-14). The card shows '[⏳ Income ₩36.7M+] ... Income: ₩36.7M a year or more (0.7× GNI). May be lower: a listed technical or skills licence instead of income.' That licence cut has factor 0. The same reader with income ₩20M and KIIP left blank goes to F-5-6 and sees '⏳ Income ₩52.4M+', although the same line lists the 70% and 60% reductions. Under those, the own-half floor is ₩18.3M or ₩15.7M, both below ₩20M. incomeFor sets 'later' from the unreduced amount: `own < amount / 2`, where amount only uses cuts whose result is 'yes'.
findings.expected: If a reduction the map cannot decide would make the reader's income enough, the verdict should be 'maybe' (no ⏳). This matches PREFER ('an unknown beats a sure not yet') and engine.md ('a fact the reader left empty ... never blocks'). Answering KIIP 5 currently gives a better verdict than leaving KIIP blank.
findings.fix: In incomeFor, compute the 'later' test against the best case. Use `const best = Math.max(Math.min(factor, ...applies.filter((c) => c.result === 'maybe').map((c) => c.factor)), floor); const low = base * best;` and set result = 'later' only when `own < low` (or `own < low / 2` under halfRule). Otherwise keep 'maybe'.

findings.title: F-2-71 -> F-3 note says a sponsor income drop moves the family to F-3 (F-3-18); the confirmed rule and F-2-71's own how text say F-1
findings.repro: /en/visa-map/#nationality=UZ&age=30&spouse=foreigner&path=F-2-71.F-3 shows 'If your F-2-7 family member no longer earns at least 1× GNI, your status changes to F-3 (F-3-18).' F-2-71's how text (line 1756) says 'Spouse or minor child of an F-2-7 holder who earns at least 1× GNI (otherwise the family gets F-1)'. F-2-71.next offers F-3 and does not offer F-1.
findings.expected: check_R1 #37 (confirmed) and check_R4b #34: when the F-2-7 holder's income is below the latest GNI, the spouse or minor child is handled as F-1. The manual's F-1 extension case is at visadocs.yaml line 9449. The 90-day F-3-18 visa is not tied to the income shortfall.
findings.fix: Point this move to F-1 with the note 'If your F-2-7 family member's income falls below 1× GNI, you are handled as F-1 (visiting family) until it is reached again'. The F-1 -> F-2-71 move already exists. Otherwise, drop the income clause from the F-3 note.

findings.title: F-2-3 and F-6-1 sponsor line says 'Your sponsor's income', but the test is the inviter's household; F-6-1 also drops the 2-person qualifier
findings.repro: /en/visa-map/#nationality=UZ&age=30&spouse=f5&path=E-9.F-2-3: the how text says 'the F-5 holder's household needs income of 1× GNI', and the computed line right after it says 'Your sponsor's income: ₩52.4M a year or more'. ru shows 'Доход приглашающего', uz 'Taklif qiluvchining daromadi'. On F-6-1 the line reads 'Your sponsor's income: ₩25.2M a year or more.', with no household size. visamap.js line 108 maps whose 'sponsor' to this one string for F-2-3, F-6-1 and F-2-71 alike.
findings.expected: R4b #29 (confirmed verbatim) and R5 #9: for F-2-3 the F-5 holder's own income or the combined income of the family living with them counts. R5 #0 and #4: for F-6-1 it is the inviter's household, ₩25,195,752 for 2 people and ₩32,154,216 for 3. Only F-2-71 is the sponsor's own income.
findings.fix: Add `household: true` beside `sponsor: true` on F-2-3 (line 1692) and F-6-1 (line 1917). In incomeLine, choose a new string vm_income_sponsor_household ('Your sponsor's household income: {amount} a year or more{rule}.') in all four i18n files when both flags are set. Put 'for 2 people' into F-6-1's rule text.

findings.title: F-2-3 how text states the child or pregnancy income waiver as fact, though the check said to drop it or mark it unconfirmed, and the computed line never offers it
findings.repro: /en/visa-map/#nationality=UZ&age=30&spouse=f5&path=E-9.F-2-3 shows 'For a spouse, the F-5 holder's household needs income of 1× GNI (70% for 3 people or fewer; not needed with a child together or a pregnancy)...', followed by 'Your sponsor's income: ₩52.4M ... May be lower: a household of 3 people or fewer: 70%.' The waiver is not listed as a possible reduction, and F-2-3 has no cut for it.
findings.expected: check_R4b discrepancy verdict #11 says: 'Drop, or mark unconfirmed, the waiver for a child or pregnancy ...: no primary source was found.' R4b #31 is 'unverifiable', and R5 #12 has confidence 0.5 and is not primary.
findings.fix: In all four languages, drop 'not needed with a child together or a pregnancy' from F-2-3's how text, or mark it as reported and unconfirmed (e.g. 'reportedly waived with a child together or a pregnancy; ask immigration').

findings.title: F-2-T in-Korea change notes show the 2x amount without its conditions, and the E-7-T note omits the ministry recommendation
findings.repro: /en/visa-map/#nationality=UZ&age=30&edu=4&rank=3&experience=0&income=110&path=E-1.F-2-T shows only 'If you meet the Top-Tier criteria. Income: ₩104.8M a year or more (2× GNI per person for 2025).' The move note replaces F-2-T's how text, so nothing on the card says why 2× applies or what else it needs. The same note is used by E-3 (983), E-7-1 (1139) and F-2-7 (1725). E-7-T (1346) says only 'After 1+ year in a high-tech field with income of at least 2× GNI.'
findings.expected: check_R4b discrepancy #9 (confirmed) and R1 #36: 2× GNI applies only after 1+ year in an advanced field at a Korean company. The applicant must meet every other Top-Tier criterion (degree, career, KIIP 1/TOPIK 1) and have a central-ministry recommendation. Otherwise the bar is 3×, or 4× with one leg missing.
findings.fix: Replace these notes with a complete text, as the E-7-S2 note already does, e.g. 'With the Top-Tier degree and career and 1+ year in a high-tech job at a Korean company: income of 2× GNI (instead of 3×), KIIP 1 or TOPIK 1 and a ministry recommendation.' Do this in all four languages.

findings.title: F-5-6 how text says income is 'lower with ... a Korean school or degree', but the confirmed reduction needs all of Korean school or a Korean bachelor's or higher
findings.repro: A reader with Korean roots and a Korean associate degree (koreanEdu=2) on F-4 reads F-5-6's how text: '(lower with KIIP 5, a Korean school or degree, or 100+ hours of volunteering)'. ru has 'корейской школе или корейском дипломе', uz 'Koreya maktabi yoki diplomi'.
